page: OVHcloud r2-60 is a memory-optimized cloud instance running on the KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on Intel Haswell architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The instance does not utilize simultaneous multithreading, assigning one dedicated thread per core. Memory allocation is configured at 60 GB, yielding a high ratio of 15 GB of RAM per core. Bundled storage includes a 100 GB local SSD, and the configuration contains zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate compute throughput typical of older generation hardware. Single-core performance is in the lower tier, recording 763.28 in stress-ng and 908.0 in Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-core performance reaches 2870.36 in stress-ng and 2740.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In memory subsystem benchmarks, uncached read bandwidth reaches 18.84 GB/s while uncached write bandwidth measures 15.46 GB/s. Despite modest compute and bandwidth ratings, the system sustains 4.47 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads.

Because compute capabilities are constrained while memory density is high, the server delivers qualitative cost efficiency primarily for memory-bound applications that do not require aggressive core performance. The r2-60 is appropriate for large-footprint in-memory key-value datastores such as Redis, caching layers, staging database replicas, and data aggregation pipelines requiring significant RAM.
description: OVHcloud r2-60 is a memory-optimized cloud instance providing 60 GB of RAM across 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by 2.2 GHz Intel Haswell processors on a KVM hypervisor. Each physical core is non-hyperthreaded and provides 15 GB of system memory, complemented by a bundled 100 GB local SSD and no GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the legacy architecture displays lower-tier compute throughput, recording 908.0 in Geekbench single-core and 2740.0 in Geekbench multi-core evaluations, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 18.84 GB/s. However, the 15:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers economical memory density for tasks where memory footprint takes precedence over per-core computation. The r2-60 is suitable for large in-memory key-value stores such as Redis, lightweight database caching layers, staging databases, and RAM-bound batch processing workloads.
